Conjugation relations of geometric and Gaussian optics

Source: R/physics-optics-gaussopt.R
geometric_conj_ab.Rd

geometric_conj_ab(a, b) is the focal distance that images a point at distance a to distance b; geometric_conj_af(a, f) and geometric_conj_bf(b, f) give the other distance from one distance and the focal distance. gaussian_conj(s_in, z_r_in, f) gives the list (s_out, z_r_out, m) for a Gaussian beam through a thin lens, and conjugate_gauss_beams(wavelen, waist_in, waist_out, f = f) the list (s_in, s_out, f) of the optical setup that conjugates two beams. After sympy.physics.optics.gaussopt.

Usage

geometric_conj_ab(a, b)

geometric_conj_af(a, f)

geometric_conj_bf(a, f)

gaussian_conj(s_in, z_r_in, f)

conjugate_gauss_beams(wavelen, waist_in, waist_out, ...)

Arguments

a, b

The distances of the object and the image.

f

The focal distance.

s_in

The distance of the waist before the lens.

z_r_in

The Rayleigh range of the incoming beam.

wavelen

The wavelength.

waist_in, waist_out

The waists of the two beams.

...

The focal distance f, the only setup supported.

Value

A sym expression or a list.

Examples

a <- Symbol("a"); b <- Symbol("b"); f <- Symbol("f")
geometric_conj_ab(a, b)
#> a*b/(a + b)
gaussian_conj(Symbol("s_in"), Symbol("z_r_in"), f)[[1]]
#> 1/(-1/(s_in + z_r_in^2/(-f + s_in)) + 1/f)
